note: NOT SHIPPED. BLOCKED, no __items.csv written. DATA DEFECT (response table): the W5 block is reordered relative to W1/W2 but the build maps it by number. _EXTEND['socialdistance'] renames W5_SocialDistance_i -> SocialDistance{i} for i=1..18. The W5 .sav variable labels AND the W5 Recontacts questionnaire (pp.41-44) insert 'I felt like people would disapprove if I didn't do it' at position 8, so W5 items 9-15 are W2 items 8-14 shifted by one and W5 16-18 are W2 15-17. Result: 8 of 24 live codes pool two different questions across waves -- SocialDistance8 (W1/W2 'I had support from others' + W5 'I felt like people would disapprove if I didn't do it'), 9 (normal and expected + support), 10 (intended + normal and expected), 11 (wanted + intended), 12 (good thing + wanted), 13 (specific plan + good thing), 14 (habit + specific plan), 18 (W2 disapprove + W5 'I felt like I could control or cope with how it made me feel so I could do it'); 2520 W5 rows each = 20,160 of 105,093 live rows. Also SocialDistance15_W5/16_W5/17_W5 hold W5 positions 15-17 = habit / bored-tired-anxious-lonely / would feel bad, not the W2 15-17 content their numbers suggest (each is internally one question, but the pooled-code fix should move them too). Evidence: live table reproduces the .sav under this positional rename cell-for-cell (53 wave-item cells, 0 mismatches), so the live data IS this mapping. Means: SocialDistance13 W1 3.61 / W2 3.66 ('plan') vs W5 4.38 (W5 label 'good thing'; W2 'good thing' = 4.40); SocialDistance14 W1 3.95 / W2 4.15 ('habit') vs W5 3.50 (W5 'plan'). Within-person W2->W5 correlations (n=948 in both waves): W5_13 'good thing' r=.526 with W2_12 'good thing' vs .216 with W2_13; W5_14 'plan' .425 with W2_13 vs .269 with W2_14; W5_15 'habit' .474 with W2_14 vs -.136 with W2_15; W5_16 'bored...' .379 with W2_15 vs .038 with W2_16; W5_8 'disapprove' .282 with W2_18 vs .231 with W2_8. Suggested crosswalk fix for W5: SocialDistance8..14 <- SocialDistance_9.._15; SocialDistance18 <- SocialDistance_8; W5 _16/_17/_18 carry the W2 15/16/17 wording verbatim (so they could pool with SocialDistance15_W2..17_W2, or keep _W5 codes sourced from _16.._18 -- builder's call). RETRY TEST: NO -- determinate verdict (a defect in the live response table, not an access failure); an unchanged retry, now, gives the same result. What would have to change: data/c19prc_uk_mcbride_2021_crosswalk.py's W5 rename for key socialdistance must map by content rather than by number, the table rebuilt and re-uploaded; after that the extraction is mechanical (all wording is in the .sav variable labels, banked at itemtext/.cache/c19prc_uk_mcbride_2021_socialdistance/label_crosswalk_by_wave.csv). Other findings for the later pass: items 1-14 have identical statements at W1 and W2; stems differ by wave (W1 '...social distancing (e.g. avoiding crowds, maintaining personal distance, avoiding non-essential meetings, less socialising in public)...', W2 '...social distancing rules (e.g. staying in your home most of the time, exercising outside once a day, not meeting up with friends and relatives, maintaining a 2-metre distance from people, working from home)...pandemic.', W5 '...social distancing practices (e.g. not entering other people's homes, maintaining a 2 metre distance from people, working from home, etc)...'); W5 item 4 reads 'I had the necessary time and facilities to do it' vs W1/W2 'I had the necessary time to do it'; W1 15-17 ('It made me feel anxious' / 'It made me feel disgusted' / 'I felt like I could control my emotional reactions so I could do it') differ from W2 15-17. Value labels 1=Strongly disagree..5=Strongly agree identical on all 53 variables, no reverse coding in the build. Rights: study-authored COM-B statements (same block family as the shipped c19prc_uk_mcbride_2021_hygiene, batch_715, adapted from COM-B-Qv1; no reserved right located there) -- not a rights issue.

note: Derivation: POSITIONAL per wave. data/c19prc_uk_mcbride_2021_crosswalk.py (key trustinstitutions, waves 1-5) renames W1 Trust_Body1..7, W2/W3 Trust_Body1..8, W4 Trust_Body1..12 and W5 Trust_Body_1..12 to institution-named codes Trust_Body_<institution>; W4/W5 inserted four items (devolved Wales/Scotland/NI, local government) at positions 3-6, shifting the rest. Header diff: the .sav variable label at every one of the 47 item-wave source positions names exactly the institution the crosswalk assigns to it (47/47; verify_c19prc_uk_mcbride_2021_trustinstitutions.R check A). Codes are also self-describing. Wording differs by wave and one text per item had to be chosen: W1-W3 labels/questionnaires read 'Parliament' and 'The government'; W4-W5 read 'The UK Parliament' and 'The UK Government'. item_text ships the W4-W5 form (the only form covering all 12 items; 6,387 of the 11,830 parliament and 11,829 government live rows are W4-W5). The other 6 shared items are worded identically in all waves. Stem: W1, W2, W4, W5 read 'Could you indicate how much trust you have in the following institutions' (no terminal punctuation) and is shipped in instructions verbatim; W3 (16,152 of 118,163 live rows) read 'Please indicate how much trust you have in the following institutions?'. resp: live table is HARMONISED by the build script to higher = more trust -- W1/W2/W4/W5 stored 1=Completely trust..5=Do not trust at all in the .sav and are recoded 6-resp; W3 stored 1=Do not trust at all..5=Completely trust and is kept raw. option_text is therefore 1=Do not trust at all, 2=Trust a little, 3=Trust moderately, 4=Trust mostly, 5=Completely trust, the .sav value-label wording (identical across waves) in live direction. Route 9: .sav item x wave x level counts after the build's reversal match the live table cell for cell in 47/47 item-waves (235 cells, 118,163 rows; e.g. W5 doctors 101/213/468/1038/700 both). SOURCE-DOC DEFECT (overridden): the measures documents state the anchor direction backwards for three waves -- 'McBride et al. (2021) measures information.docx' 2.2.12.2 says W3 was scored 1='completely trust' to 5='do not trust at all', and 'C19PRC W4 Supplementary Measures Material.docx' 2.2.10 and the W5 equivalent 2.2.6.4 say 1='do not trust at all' to 5='completely trust' -- each the opposite of that wave's .sav value labels. The .sav labels win on the data: raw codes of the same respondents correlate negatively exactly across the boundaries where the .sav labels flip (doctors W2 vs W3 r=-0.59 n=947; W3 vs W4 r=-0.62 n=1431) and positively where they do not (W1 vs W2 +0.57 n=1401; W4 vs W5 +0.64 n=2377); police and political parties show the same pattern. After harmonisation doctors are the most trusted item (live mean 3.83) and political parties the least (2.20) in every wave. (The W4/W5 questionnaire PDFs display the grid left-to-right Do not trust at all..Completely trust, the reverse of the stored codes -- display order, not coding.) The W1 questionnaire PDF is image-only and was not read; W1 wording rests on the .sav labels and the codebook, which match W2. Rights: study-authored question block; the measures docs cite no source instrument for it. No register row applies; no fee/permission/NC/ND/redistribution clause located -- silence, extracted from the study's own CC BY 4.0 deposit. English administration (UK), no language/_translated columns.
public_note: Two institutions were worded differently across waves -- waves 1-3 read 'Parliament' and 'The government' where waves 4-5 (shipped) read 'The UK Parliament' and 'The UK Government' -- and the wave 3 prompt read 'Please indicate how much trust you have in the following institutions?'; resp is harmonised so 5 = Completely trust in every wave, although waves 1, 2, 4 and 5 were stored in the opposite direction in the source files.
